neighbours.label: ' on' after put, set, send or continue when a path noun follows (on track, on a trajectory, on the road to, on a collision course), as opposed to ' on' for a place or a surface
fire: The new budget should put the school on track to reopen by May.
That burn sent the probe on a long arc around the moon.
Her first novel set her on the road to fame.
If voters continue on this course, the party will split.
A single meeting can put a startup on a path to profit.
The reforms placed the economy on a steady upward path.
His tweets have put him on a collision course with the board.
An early mentor set the young chemist on her career path.
quiet: The new budget was left on the table until May.
That burn left a mark on a long stretch of the moon rock.
Her first novel sat on the shelf by the door.
If voters stand on this corner, the police will come.
A single meeting can be held on a Tuesday at noon.
The reforms were printed on a large poster downtown.
His tweets appeared on a screen behind the board.
An early mentor hung the young chemist's diploma on her wall.
